$note: coding 模式的工具表：七个。exec_command 是 destructive + open-world，不因为某次命令看着安全就改注解。

tools.name: workspace_info
tools.description: Name, git status and platform of the remote workspace. Call once to orient; all other tool paths are relative to this workspace.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file from the remote workspace, as numbered lines. Paths are relative to the workspace root. Long files come back truncated with the line to resume from; there is no way to read a file whole in one call.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List a directory of the remote workspace, or search it with a glob. Without a glob you get the immediate children of one directory; with one you get every match under it, at any depth. In a git workspace, files that .gitignore rules out are never listed.

tools.name: search_text
tools.description: Search the remote workspace for a string, or a regex if you ask for one. The search runs where the files are and only the matching lines come back. Files that .gitignore rules out, dotfiles and .git are never searched.

tools.name: read_output
tools.description: Page through what a command wrote, using the output_ref exec_command returned. Offsets are byte offsets and stable: a finished command's output does not change.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: Change files in the remote workspace: add, update, delete or move. This is the only way to write. An update replaces exact strings and must carry the version read_file returned, so an edit built on content that has since changed is refused. Either every file in the patch is applied or none is.

tools.name: exec_command
tools.description: Run a command in the remote workspace. cmd is a program and its arguments, not a shell line: there are no pipes, redirection or globs. Long output stays on that machine; what comes back is the head and tail plus an output_ref. This runs with the full access of the account the runtime uses.
